clue.text: Before ultimate promotion in army time zone?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
C-in-C, Commander-in-Chief, is the highest rank a soldier can reach

explanation.surface: A soldier asks what time zone the top brass work in.
explanation.walkthrough: CINC is Commander-in-Chief, the top of the army ladder, so the 'promotion' is a rank, not a career move.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is an enclosed area or district, so it is a kind of zone; the question mark admits the looseness.

clue.text: First rather than last vowel in "longer pitch expert"

indicators.note: in tells us the middle phrase sits inside the word for one who longs

parts.note: a longer is someone who longs, a piner
A is the first vowel of the alphabet
A rather than U reads as A not U
U is the last of the five vowels

explanation.surface: A phonetician quotes a phrase and asks which vowel to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longer' is one who longs, not the comparative of long. 'First rather than last vowel' must be read word by word as a little phrase, and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner adjusts strings to the correct pitch, a specialist in exact tuning.

clue.text: Soap festivals aim to provide a break

indicators.note: breaking into something means interrupting it, so the aim goes inside the festivals

parts.note: Easter is a festival; Easters is the plural
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A soap opera aims to give its viewers a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC television soap opera set in east London; 'to provide a break' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC serial set in east London is one of Britain's best-known television soaps.

clue.text: Setter's surgeon's feet

parts.note: the setter speaks as I, and setter's reads as setter is, I am
BS is Bachelor of Surgery, a surgeon's degree

explanation.surface: A setter mentions their surgeon's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is the setter is, so I AM; feet are units of poetic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of an unstressed then a stressed syllable.

clue.text: Epergnes providing aim of grandmaster's gambit?

definitions.meaning: an epergne is an ornamental table stand for fruit or flowers
a chess gambit sacrifices material to get pieces into the middle of the board

explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' only joins the two definitions; a chess gambit gives up a pawn for central control.
explanation.definitionFit: Epergnes are decorative table centrepieces, and controlling the centre with pieces is a gambit's purpose.

clue.text: Increased the pain to the ear's capacity to accept

indicators.note: something heard by the ear is a word judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to increase is to up, and pain is ache: upped ache

explanation.surface: Someone's ear pain worsens just as their hearing is tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the ear' says that 'upped ache', a paraphrase of 'Increased the pain', is said aloud to give the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptake is absorption or the ability to take something in, whether nutrients or ideas.

clue.text: See 7
One intoxicated by smart books used in combating mental disorders

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple
tipsy means slightly drunk

indicators.note: used in means the books are put inside the smart piece

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish
OT, Old Testament, is the crossword abbreviation for books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A drunk is dosed with smart books meant to help with mental illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' is the container signal and 'by' only joins; the surface's drunk and smart books are a picture, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipsychotic drugs combat psychosis, a severe group of mental disorders.

clue.text: Service of just a trifle

parts.note: even means fair or just
a song is a trifling sum, as in going for a song

explanation.surface: A service of fairness is offered for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' means for very little, so SONG is a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Church of England.

clue.text: Once arrogant aims to get guns dismantled

indicators.note: dismantled things are taken apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A conceited army sets out to have its weapons taken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismantled' rearranges the eight letters of AIMS and GUNS together; 'to get' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming once meant presumptuous or arrogant, a sense now dated, hence 'Once'.

clue.text: Termly this flower girl comes out

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerging in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl comes out of school each term like a flower opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' rearranges TERMLY; 'this' is a link, pointing at the answer as the flower girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is both an evergreen flowering shrub and a girl's first name.

clue.text: S-some love might be described thus

definitions.text: S-some love might be described thus

parts.words: S-some love might be described thus
parts.note: the stammered S is the first glimpse of the word some, and some love begins in this way on first meeting

explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is the key: the S appears first, before 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes love that strikes on first meeting, and the stutter shows the S seen first.

clue.text: Exaggerate on the subject of time

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over money
a stretch is a period of time, especially a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Someone protests against overstating how long something takes.
explanation.walkthrough: STRETCH is slang for a term in prison, so 'time' is the convict's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstretch a claim or argument is to push it too far, to overstate or exaggerate it.

clue.text: Strip out of clothing — in case I decrease in importance

indicators.note: a word out of its clothing has lost its outer letters
in places the letter I inside the travelling case

parts.note: a valise is a small suitcase

explanation.surface: A stripper takes off their clothes while a suitcase shrinks in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of clothing' strips the word Strip of its outer letters, and 'in' sets I inside the case to give VIALISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trivialise something is to treat it as less important than it is.

clue.text: Crosses alarm shy birdies

indicators.note: alarming the birds makes them scatter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a golf course and startles timid birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarm' scatters SHY and BIRDIES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hybridises is to crossbreed, so crosses as in mating different varieties.

clue.text: Like someone sleeping with insurance agent in secret?

definitions.meaning: a sleeper lies beneath the bedclothes
being insured means having ... against loss
a spy works covertly, in disguise

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: the bed, the insurance policy and the spy each give the same two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the covers, under insurance cover, and covert spying all share the one phrase meaning concealed or protected.

clue.text: Interpretation of material on paper makes Thatcher cross

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters make up something new, an anagram

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's reading annoys Mrs Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges THATCHER and CROSS; Margaret Thatcher was the British prime minister of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The inkblot test asks subjects to interpret ink patterns printed on cards.

clue.text: Corrupt party with line that's not simply black and white?

definitions.text: that's not simply black and white?

indicators.note: something corrupted has been spoilt and altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party bends its line on issues that are not clear-cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges PARTY and LINE together; 'with' only joins. The definition plays on a painting being in colour rather than mere outline.
explanation.definitionFit: Painterly describes art using colour and brushwork rather than line, so it is more than black and white drawing.

clue.text: Pope's non-human?

parts.note: Alexander Pope wrote 'to err is human', so anyone who never makes a mistake would by his measure not be human; a papal reading of infallibility also hovers

explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pope, an eighteenth-century English poet, wrote 'To err is human, to forgive divine'; the capital P also suggests the Pope and his claimed infallibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Errorless means without mistakes, and Pope linked making mistakes with being human.

clue.text: See 15
Course is very large — what's backed in the day's races

indicators.note: placed in means the reversed pair goes inside the race card

parts.note: a race card lists the day's races at a meeting

indicators.note: something backed goes backwards, so the pair of words is turned round

parts.note: obese means very fat
eh? is a way of asking what's that

explanation.surface: A racing tipster says the course is huge and asks what horse to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the pair into HEESEBO, which 'in' places inside the day's racecard; 'is' is a link. A card lists the races at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseboard is served as a course of a meal, after dessert or in place of it.

clue.text: PM accounting for British Rail's ruin

indicators.note: ruin wrecks the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A prime minister is blamed for the ruin of British Rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' rearranges RAIL to LAIR; British Rail was the old nationalised train company.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was the UK prime minister from 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: See 8
See 16
Old and new forever requiring no reciprocal action

parts.note: ay or aye is a poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Old and new are united in a lasting arrangement that needs nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: AY is an archaic word for ever or always, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way arrangement works in one direction only, with nothing given back.

clue.text: Either of two early saints suiting a change

indicators.note: a change of clothes or order means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor says an outfit suits either saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SUITING plus A, eight letters; the tailoring surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ignatius of Antioch and Saint Ignatius of Loyola are the best-known saints of that name.

clue.text: "Had tea delivered!", as triumphant hoaxer shouts

indicators.note: a line delivered is spoken aloud, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: had means got, and char is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having had their tea brought to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' says that 'got char', a paraphrase of 'Had tea', is spoken aloud; char is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a contraction of got you, crowed when catching someone out.

clue.text: "Naked king and queen", read in horoscope

indicators.note: something read in a source is found inside it, so these go within the other piece

parts.note: a horoscope is often called the stars
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A tabloid horoscope predicts nudity for a royal couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read in' is the container signal: what you read in your horoscope sits inside it. Starkers is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for stark naked.
